name: SC-06
label: Safe D

key_factors: Prediction markets price Clyburn near-certain to win
model.rationale: Clyburn holds a D+13 district with a big fundraising edge and no serious polling or ratings suggesting vulnerability, while markets price him at roughly 95% to win. The fundamentals point to a comfortable double-digit Democratic margin.
model.watch: A major late-breaking scandal or unexpectedly strong Republican outside spending could narrow the margin, though not likely enough to threaten the seat.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
South Carolina's 6th District is a safely Democratic seat anchored in Columbia and the majority-Black Lowcountry corridor. Jim Clyburn, the longtime incumbent and a House Democratic leader, is running for reelection with more than $1.6 million on hand, while Republican John Peterson has reported minimal fundraising and little outside support. No general-election polls or expert ratings track the race, so the outlook rests on fundamentals.

The district's D+13 partisan lean, Clyburn's incumbency advantage, and his financial edge all point to a comfortable Democratic win in the low-to-mid twenties margin. Prediction markets likewise price Clyburn as an overwhelming favorite. Barring extraordinary developments, the seat is expected to remain in Democratic hands.
